# Web design craft

Begin with the content and the task. A portfolio, editorial story, product settings page and
commerce landing page require different compositions. Avoid choosing the same centered hero,
three cards and purple gradient merely because the brief is open-ended.

- Establish an explicit hierarchy: one dominant action, readable supporting copy, quieter metadata.
  Use scale, grouping, whitespace and alignment before adding boxes or decoration.
- Pick a type rhythm with a small set of sizes and weights. Keep body lines around 65–75 characters.
  Static previews have system fonts: use deliberate serif/sans contrast or a consistent product sans
  instead of naming unavailable fonts. Test long titles, numbers and real button labels.
- Choose a restrained or intentionally expressive palette from the brief. Check readable text on
  every surface, visible keyboard focus and meaningful state differences beyond color alone.
- Make spacing express relationships. Related controls belong closer together than separate tasks.
  Avoid nested cards, decorative border stripes and identical spacing for every section.
- Design narrow layouts structurally: stack columns, change navigation treatment, preserve action
  visibility and reading order. Avoid fixed widths that force horizontal scrolling.
- Use supplied photography or illustration intentionally. If none exists, choose a convincing
  typography-led composition rather than inventing product screenshots or fake visual assets.
- Forms, dashboards and transactional UIs must distinguish example data from persisted outcomes.
  A static concept can depict states, but cannot claim that a payment, save or connection occurred.

Keep DESIGN.md short enough to guide the next iteration. Record decisions and evidence, not a
catalogue of every CSS declaration. References from another project apply only when requested.
